_comment: Router-template signatures. Each signature is self-proving: agent-police
reports the response evidence that matched, not a claim from a list. Add
your own with --signatures. 'confidence' describes how specific the
evidence is to that software, not how sure we are that it is malicious -
running any of these is completely normal and is not itself a finding.
A signature only matches if at least one STRONG check matches. A strong
body_contains); a bare status check is weak, because routers that serve a
single-page app answer 200 with the same shell for every unknown path.
Every check is additionally discarded if its response is indistinguishable
from the endpoint's measured catch-all response.

signatures.name: LiteLLM proxy
signatures.note: Open-source router; the March 2026 dependency-confusion compromise gave the injected code write access to every transiting request.

signatures.name: one-api / new-api family
signatures.note: The two templates that underpin most commodity resale routers (arXiv:2604.08407 section 2.1). Calibrated against a live new-api deployment: /api/status returns JSON with success=true and a data object.

signatures.name: sub2api
signatures.note: Template behind a large share of the free-router corpus measured in the paper.

signatures.name: CLIProxyAPI
signatures.note: Deployed as a weak-password decoy in the paper's poisoning study.

signatures.name: claude-relay-service
signatures.note: Relay software used across 20 decoy domains in the paper's poisoning study.
